title: test: add empty-input and blank-line tests
author: priya-learns
description:
Adds two missing tests:
- `test_empty_input` — confirms `render('')` returns `''`
- `test_blank_lines_ignored` — confirms blank lines between blocks don't produce output

No linked issue. I noticed these cases weren't covered while reading through the test file.

**Changes:**
- `tests/test_mdlite.py`: 2 test functions added

**Testing:**
- All existing tests still pass
- Both new tests pass

review_comments.author: riya-dev
review_comments.body: Nice addition — these edge cases should definitely be covered. Merging.

lesson_note: No linked issue, no bug to fix — just a contributor who read the test file, noticed a gap, and filled it cleanly. Small scope, passes CI, maintainer merged same day. You don't need a bug report to make a useful contribution.

title: fix: strip trailing spaces from headings
author: dev-rohan
description:
Headings with trailing spaces produce output like `

Hello

`. This strips them. **Changes:** - `src/mdlite.py`: `.rstrip()` added to the text slice in each heading branch **Testing:** - Added `test_heading_trailing_space` in `tests/test_mdlite.py` - All existing tests pass
diff_summary: src/mdlite.py: changed line[2:] to line[2:].rstrip() (and equivalents for h2, h3)

review_comments.author: ci-bot
review_comments.body: `black --check` failed on `src/mdlite.py`. Please run `black src/ tests/` before pushing.

review_comments.author: riya-dev
review_comments.body: The change looks correct but CI is red. Can you run `black src/ tests/` and push the result?

review_comments.author: dev-rohan
review_comments.body: Done — pushed a formatting commit. CI is green now.

review_comments.author: riya-dev
review_comments.body: Perfect. Clean diff, test included, CI passing. Merging — thanks!

lesson_note: CI failed on the first push because of formatting. The maintainer didn't reject the PR — they asked for one specific fix. The contributor ran black, pushed the result, and the PR merged cleanly. A CI failure on your first push is normal; what matters is how you respond to it.
